title: Oracle bans AI-generated code from OpenJDK
titleZh: Oracle 禁止 OpenJDK 中人工智能生成的代码
author: delduca
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Oracle has banned AI-generated code from OpenJDK contributions, citing safety, security, and intellectual property risks. The open-source Java project steward said developers can use LLMs privately for debugging and reviewing code but cannot submit AI-generated material to repositories, pull requests, or other project channels.

The policy contrasts sharply with Oracle's internal practices. Co-founder Larry Ellison recently declared that AI models now write Oracle's code, whilst co-CEO Mike Sicilia credited AI tools with enabling smaller engineering teams to deliver faster.

Oracle is investing $70 billion this year in datacentre expansion. The spending spree prompted credit agency S&P to downgrade Oracle's rating to BBB-, one notch above junk status, citing uncertain returns on investment.Source: theregister.com

comments.author: jerf
comments.textRawHtml: Oracle, the law firm with a tech business attached, probably wants to retain the option to sue other people for AI-washing their proprietary code, and that doesn't work if they're also publicly accepting AI contributions to their code with no apparent concern for the provenance of it. The tech business would probably tell them this isn't going to be a needle they are going to be able to successfully thread, but the law firm is in the driver's seat.
comments.textZhHtml: 甲骨文（Oracle）是一家附属于科技业务的律师事务所，它可能希望保留起诉其他人对其专有代码进行人工智能清洗的选择，但如果他们也公开接受人工智能对其代码的贡献，而没有明显关心其来源，那么这种选择就行不通。科技行业可能会告诉他们，这不会成为他们能够成功穿线的针，但律师事务所处于主导地位。

children.author: TimTheTinker
children.textRawHtml:
What I don't understand is why anyone with half a brain would even venture to touch Oracle with a ten foot pole given that they've had this reputation for at least the last 25 years.

Why, people?
children.textZhHtml:
我不明白的是，为什么任何有半点脑子的人都会冒险用一根 10 英尺长的杆子去触碰 Oracle，因为 Oracle 已经享有这样的声誉至少 25 年了。

为什么，朋友们？

children.author: KronisLV
children.textRawHtml:
> Why, people?

As someone who's had to use the Oracle database and also Oracle Linux on servers, beats me. Also stuff like Oracle ADF and JDeveloper and JBoss/WildFly, no thank you.

I seriously hope someone got bribed to choose Oracle cause it doesn't make sense otherwise, at least then they would have gotten something good out of it.

The closest thing to an actual argument I've heard was wanting paid support - in which case let me introduce to KronisCo (which will be registered shortly) and if you only give me fat coffeurs of money, I will provide similar support for PostgreSQL with the added benefits of your developers not wanting to retire at 30. Like why would anyone pay for Oracle in the first place, when they can just collect that cheque themselves and freeload on battle-tested FOSS (or contribute back)? Seeing a software dev org just pass those sums to Oracle from their clients without trying to capture that seemed wild.
children.textZhHtml:
> 为什么，朋友们？

作为一个必须在服务器上使用 Oracle 数据库和 Oracle Linux 的人，这让我感到困惑。还有像 Oracle ADF 和 JDeveloper 和 JBoss/WildFly 这样的东西，不，谢谢。

我真的希望有人被贿赂选择 Oracle，因为否则就没有意义，至少他们会从中得到一些好东西。

我听到的最接近实际争论的是想要付费支持 - 在这种情况下，让我介绍一下 KronisCo（很快就会注册），如果你只给我胖的话如果你有钱，我将为 PostgreSQL 提供类似的支持，并为你的开发人员提供额外的好处，他们不想在 30 岁退休。就像为什么任何人首先为 Oracle 付费，因为他们可以自己收集支票并免费使用经过考验的 FOSS（或回馈）？看到软件开发组织只是将这些金额从客户那里传递给 Oracle，而不尝试捕获，这似乎很疯狂。

children.author: nnevatie
children.textRawHtml: Ahhaha. JBoss, the glorified web-app server that booted for tens of minutes. It was the peak of Java-based over-engineering.
children.textZhHtml: 啊哈哈。 JBoss，一款备受赞誉的网络应用服务器，启动时间长达数十分钟。这是基于 Java 的过度工程的顶峰。

children.author: bzzzt
children.textRawHtml:
And it's not even an Oracle product. If you want that from them you need WebLogic.

To be fair, recent versions of JBoss/Wildfly removed a lot of the bloat and boot within seconds. Startup time is mostly due to application frameworks nowadays.
children.textZhHtml:
而且它甚至不是 Oracle 产品。如果您想从他们那里获得这些，您需要 WebLogic。

公平地说，JBoss/Wildfly 的最新版本消除了很多臃肿并在几秒钟内启动。现在的启动时间主要取决于应用程序框架。

children.author: doubled112
children.textRawHtml:
This conversation just dug some old nightmares out.

In a past life, I used to be almost ecstatic when a client would choose Tomcat over WebLogic or WebSphere, or whatever abomination of an app server they standardized on.
children.textZhHtml:
这次对话只是挖出了一些旧的噩梦。

在过去的生活中，当客户选择 Tomcat 而不是 WebLogic 或 WebSphere，或者他们标准化的任何令人厌恶的应用服务器时，我几乎欣喜若狂。

children.textZhHtml: 因为我的老板喜欢高尔夫球场，而且在 Oracle 销售代表付费的情况下更喜欢。

children.author: TimTheTinker
children.textRawHtml:
Wait, Oracle sales reps give decision-makers personal kickbacks for buying Oracle??

Stay classy Oracle. Such a banal depth of evil.

Why hasn't this been outlawed?

I guess companies that knowingly employ such managers deserve to lose whatever Oracle's legal team extracts out of them.
children.textZhHtml:
等等，Oracle 销售代表为购买 Oracle 的决策者提供个人回扣？？

保持优雅的 Oracle。如此平庸的邪恶。

为什么这种行为没有被取缔？

我想，故意雇用此类经理的公司应该失去甲骨文法律团队从他们身上榨取的一切。

children.author: smuhakg
children.textRawHtml:

https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2022-173

This is why corporate procurement in a large enterprise is so bureaucratic. If you have 20 layers of approval that's 20 people that need cocaine and prostitutes yet could blow the whistle.
children.textZhHtml:

https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2022-173

这就是为什么大企业的采购如此官僚化。如果你有 20 层批准，那么就有 20 个人需要可卡因和妓女，但可以举报。

children.author: preg_match
children.textRawHtml:
One of the worst side-effects of corruption and cronyism isn't even the corruption part, it's the insane administrative cost it inevitably breeds in process in order to try to fix.

This is largely why the US government is so inefficient. Our government agencies have been trained to outsource absolutely everything. A static site? No, you couldn't possibly hire one or two engineers to do that, you need a multi-million dollar contract! Well, when you do that, the corruption risk is through the roof. Now we mitigate with anti-corruption, anti-fraud checks out the fucking wazoo. That's expensive. And we're putting that expense ON TOP of the exorbitant contract fees.
children.textZhHtml:
腐败和任人唯亲的最严重副作用之一甚至不是腐败部分，而是在试图解决问题的过程中不可避免地产生的疯狂的行政成本。

这在很大程度上是美国政府效率如此低下的原因。我们的政府机构接受过完全外包一切的培训。静态网站？不，你不可能雇佣一两个工程师来做到这一点，你需要一份数百万美元的合同！好吧，当你这样做时，腐败风险就会达到顶峰。现在我们通过反腐败、反欺诈来缓解这种情况。那很贵。我们将这笔费用放在高昂的合同费用之上。

children.author: inigyou
children.textRawHtml:
Pretty much every business does this to acquire large corporate and government customers.

Every customer acquisition will be weeks or months of in-person discussions over golf, expensive dinners, resort vacations, or the like.
children.textZhHtml:
几乎每个企业都这样做是为了获取大型企业和政府客户。

每次获取客户都需要数周或数月的时间，就高尔夫、昂贵的晚餐、度假胜地度假等进行面对面的讨论。

children.author: xyzzy_plugh
children.textRawHtml:
You've clearly never purchased enterprise software at scale before. Oracle doesn't do anything that everyone else isn't already doing.

Dinners, drinks, bottles of scotch, tickets to baseball and football games, plane tickets to attend training sessions in conference rooms attached to nice beachside hotels, business lunches at strip clubs, Superbowl tickets, cruise tickets, wristwatches...

Not to mention mugs, tshirts, water bottles and stickers.

Everything is on the menu.
children.textZhHtml:
您显然以前从未大规模购买过企业软件。 Oracle 不会做任何其他人都没有做过的事情。

晚餐、饮料、瓶装苏格兰威士忌、棒球和足球比赛的门票、参加漂亮海滨酒店附属会议室培训课程的机票、脱衣舞俱乐部的商务午餐、超级碗门票、游轮门票、手表...

更不用说杯子、T 恤、水瓶和贴纸。

一切都在菜单上。

children.author: lenkite
children.textRawHtml: Our company has a strict gift giving and no-bribes policy. Everyone needs to sign that they have read it. It is even more extensive for the sales/procurement teams.
children.textZhHtml: 我们公司有严格的送礼和反贿赂政策。每个人都需要签名表示已阅读该内容。对于销售/采购团队来说，它的范围更为广泛。

children.author: xyzzy_plugh
children.textRawHtml:
Of course, I signed many such agreements. I've also turned down a ton of "gifts" such as these.

But oftentimes they are not clearly gifts or bribes. For example, inviting you or your team out for dinner and drinks can be harmless.

It's not unusual to take clients out, even to sporting events. As long as the host party is present, and there is intent to network or discuss business, it usually qualifies as "corporate hospitality" -- even the strip club!

All expensed and paid for out of the marketing budget. A far cry from gifts or bribes, apparently!
children.textZhHtml:
当然，我签署了很多这样的协议。我也拒绝过大量诸如此类的“礼物”。

但通常它们并不明显是礼物或贿赂。例如，邀请您或您的团队出去吃饭和喝酒可能是无害的。

带客户出去，甚至参加体育赛事，这并不罕见。只要主办方在场，并且有建立联系或讨论业务的意图，它通常就符合“公司招待”的资格 - 甚至是脱衣舞俱乐部！

所有费用均在营销预算之外支付。显然，这与礼物或贿赂相去甚远！
